en: Advayavajra’s Works 22. *Tattvadaśaka*,
edited by Mahāmahopādhyāya Hara Prasād Śāstrī.
In the *Advayavajrasaṃgraha*, edited by the Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai and published as GOS 1927 in Baroda;
and in the *Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō*.
Homage again and again to Suchness, which is devoid of the conjunction of existence and non-existence.
Because that very [nature] is undisturbed, it is, through awakening, of the nature of enlightenment. || 1 ||
For one who wishes to know suchness, it is neither with form nor without form; it is the Middle Way, indeed the very Middle Way, unadorned by the words of a teacher. (2)
That awakening would be an entity once attachment has been abandoned by its very nature;
attachment is born from delusion, and delusion is considered to be without a locus. (3)
What is the reality? It is the nature of the thing, since form is that from which formlessness arises;
and formlessness becomes form by virtue of the intrinsic nature of cause and effect. (4)
Thus all these phenomena are of a single flavor, unattached, and without foundation;
they are all luminous through the samādhi of reality as it is.
And through the mind of setting forth (*prasthānacitta*), there arises the samādhi of reality as it is;
for from that, reality is born incessantly for those who know that state. (6)
The world itself, devoid of both knowledge and the object of knowledge, is considered non-dual;
likewise, the very conceit of being devoid of duality is indeed luminosity. (7)
By means of this awakening to reality, in whatever way and by whatever path,
the yogi may wander everywhere with eyes wide open, like a lion.
Transcending the worldly dharmas, he has taken up the vow of a madman;
adorned by self-consecration, he acts without any support.
The stainless reality that has been described, which is called non-dual—having abandoned both the equal and the unequal, those rich in wisdom ought to know it. (10)
Farewell.
